claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic, as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying a thin oxide-forming-element coating can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminum or silicon is a suitable coating choice for this intervention.
The proposed intervention is the addition of a thin oxide-forming-element coating.
The hypothesis is scoped to 800 °C in air for 5 hours without external loading.
The coating will produce a protective oxide layer.
The coating element reacts with oxygen to form the protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer prevents or limits reaction between oxygen and the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen reaction with the underlying alloy reduces oxidation.
Relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr, the coated material will have improved oxygen resistance and reduced oxidation.
The coating may improve high-temperature mechanical properties.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr is the comparison baseline.
The effectiveness of the coating and its effect on mechanical properties are uncertain.
A controlled exposure experiment comparing coated and untreated material can test the hypothesis using oxidation rate and mechanical-property measurements.

contradictions.description: Improvement in high-temperature mechanical properties is described only as potential, but the falsification rule treats lack of improvement in mechanical properties as a possible basis for falsification. A non-required outcome should not determine falsification.
